concepts.why: The presence of angiofibromas, renal disease, and skin lesions supports this diagnosis.
The histologic analysis showing a dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels is consistent with angiofibroma.
The electron microscopy showing dermal fibroblasts with crystalline inclusions supports this diagnosis.
The presence of conical teeth is a characteristic feature of certain genetic disorders.
The patient's history of requiring a renal transplant is relevant to the diagnosis.
The presence of skin-colored papules is consistent with fibrofolliculoma.
The combination of conical teeth and renal disease suggests a possible diagnosis of MEN1.
The presence of conical teeth is a feature of NF1, although other diagnostic criteria are not met in this case.
